Convert Linked Bird Records into Paired Distance-Removal Counts

Source: R/prepare_gdr_histories.R
prepare_gdr_histories.Rd

Turn a matrix of bird records, one row per individual at a survey, into the distance and removal count tables of a distance-removal model. The function finds each bird's first detection across all distance bands, including bands beyond the survey radius, before it applies the radius. It keeps every source record, reports what happened to each bird, and never deletes or repairs a record.

Usage

prepare_gdr_histories(
  histories,
  history_keys,
  event_keys,
  event_id,
  individual_id,
  cell_map,
  dist_breaks,
  radius,
  interval_lengths,
  interval_units,
  units_in,
  surveyed,
  expected_event_keys = NULL,
  native_frame = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'msr_gdr_histories'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

histories

Numeric or logical matrix with one row per individual bird at a survey and one named column per source cell (one distance band in one time interval). Enter 1 where the bird was recorded and 0 elsewhere. Any other value, including NA, is kept as it is and reported in findings; it is never treated as 0.

history_keys

Data frame with one row per row of histories, in the same order, holding the original survey and individual identifiers and any other notes you want to keep.

event_keys

Data frame with one row per survey event, in the order the count tables should have. Include completed surveys that recorded no birds. Event keys must be unique.

event_id

Character vector naming the column(s) that identify a survey in both event_keys and history_keys.

individual_id

Character vector naming the column(s) of history_keys that identify a bird within a survey. Each survey and individual combination must be unique.

cell_map

Data frame with columns column (a column name of histories), interval and distance_bin (positive whole numbers). It must map every column of histories to exactly one combination of interval and distance band, and every combination must appear once. Columns of histories can be in any order.

dist_breaks

Increasing distance boundaries of the source bands, starting at zero, in units_in. Include bands beyond the survey radius when the records have them. Only the last boundary may be Inf.

radius

Survey radius, in units_in. It must equal one of dist_breaks, because a band cannot be split without finer distances.

interval_lengths

Positive whole numbers giving the duration of each time interval, in interval_units. Intervals may differ in length.

interval_units

Character string naming the time unit, such as "seconds". It is recorded, not converted.

units_in

Distance units of dist_breaks and radius, "m" or "km".

surveyed

Logical vector with one value per event, in event order, with no NA: TRUE for a completed survey and FALSE for an event that was not surveyed. A recorded bird at an unsurveyed event is an error.

expected_event_keys

Optional data frame, built independently, with the event_id columns in the intended event order. The function stops if event_keys differs from it.

native_frame

Optional single-visit unmarkedFrameGDR built earlier from these records. It is audited with validate_unmarked_data(), and the function stops unless its two count tables, its distance boundaries up to the radius and its interval lengths match the prepared results exactly. Distances in meters and kilometers are compared in meters, without changing either input.

x

A prepared msr_gdr_histories object.

...

Not used.

Value

A list of class msr_gdr_histories:

  • histories, history_keys, event_keys and cell_map: the inputs, unchanged.

  • first: one row per bird, with its row in histories (.history_row), its event (.event), the first interval with a recorded mark (candidate_interval), the resolved first detection (first_interval, first_distance_bin; NA when unresolved), whether the bird is counted (primary_eligible), whether every cell holds a valid 0 or 1 with at most one band per interval (history_complete), whether both hold (complete_history_eligible) and its status (see "Read the status of each bird").

  • events: one row per event, with surveyed, response_complete (whether its counts are observed), known_first_records (birds counted) and unresolved_first_histories.

  • findings: one row per problem, with the history row, the cell (.cell, .column, interval, distance_bin), a code and the original value. Findings about a whole history have missing cell fields.

  • first_cells: counts of first detections by event (rows) and cell inside the radius (columns), ordered by distance band, then interval.

  • native_cells: the rows of cell_map for those columns, in the same order.

  • yDistance and yRemoval: the two count tables, events by distance band and events by interval, ready for unmarked::unmarkedFrameGDR().

  • protocol: the source and in-radius distance breaks, the radius, units, interval lengths and the column order of first_cells.

  • surveyed, survey_audit (the audit of native_frame, or NULL), fingerprint (a SHA-256 of the inputs) and summary (counts of histories, events, counted birds, complete histories, invalid cells, unresolved events and birds first detected outside the radius).

  • fit_eligibility_established and density_identification_established: always FALSE. Preparing counts does not show that a model fitted to them is valid.

Printing reports the summary counts and returns the object invisibly. Errors in the inputs stop with a condition of class msr_gdr_history_error whose history_rows element lists the rows involved, when they are known.

Find each bird's first detection

The first detection is found across all source bands before the radius is applied. A bird first recorded beyond the radius stays out of the counts, even if a later mark places it near the point. If a bird has marks in more than one distance band in the same interval, its distance in that interval is not unique. Such marks are kept for review and never collapsed into one band. They may call for a model of movement or of the recording process.

A bird is counted when its first detection is known and inside the radius, even if a later mark is malformed. That bird is then left out of the complete-history subset. When a malformed or multi-band mark falls at or before a bird's first detection, the first detection is unresolved, as it is for a history with a malformed mark and no detection. The whole event's counts then become missing, so that an incomplete count cannot pass as an observed zero. The known partial count stays in events$known_first_records, and the source rows stay in histories.

Read the status of each bird

statusMeaning
retained_firstCounted. The history is complete
retained_first_incomplete_historyCounted, but a later mark is malformed or spans two bands
first_outside_radiusNot counted. The bird was first detected beyond the radius
unresolved_firstThe first detection cannot be determined. The event's counts are missing
no_recordNo detections were recorded, and every cell is a valid 0
unsurveyed_historyThe history belongs to an event that was not surveyed

findings uses the codes invalid_mark (a cell that is not 0 or 1, with its value), multiple_distance_bins (marks in more than one band in an interval), and unresolved_first, first_outside_radius and unsurveyed_history as in the table.

Read the count tables

Summing the columns of first_cells over intervals gives yDistance, and summing over distance bands gives yRemoval, so the two tables always have equal row totals. A completed survey with no counted birds has a row of zeros. An unsurveyed event, or an event with an unresolved bird, has a row of NA.

Keep the other responses separate

The paired first detections are one response. Complete linked histories of the counted birds, re-detections, and marks beyond the radius are others. Their likelihoods have different constants and conditioning, so they cannot be compared in one AIC table. The time intervals within one count are also not independent visits. Keep the source records for any separate analysis. Better records of the detected birds do not by themselves identify the birds that were never detected.

See the "Prepare your own records" section of vignette("v12-distance-removal", package = "multiScaleR") for a worked example.

See also

validate_unmarked_data(), prepare_gdr_intervals(), expand_gdr_intervals()

Examples

# Source cells: 2 time intervals by 3 distance bands (0-25 m, 25-75 m and
# beyond the 75 m radius)
map <- expand.grid(interval = 1:2, distance_bin = 1:3)
map$column <- paste0("cell", 1:6)
h <- matrix(0, 2, 6, dimnames = list(NULL, map$column))
h[1, c(5, 2)] <- 1 # Beyond 75 m first, then near: not counted
h[2, 1] <- 1       # Interval 1, 0-25 m: counted
h[2, 2] <- 2       # Malformed later mark: the valid first still counts
prepared <- prepare_gdr_histories(h,
  history_keys = data.frame(survey = c("a", "a"), bird = c("one", "two")),
  event_keys = data.frame(survey = c("a", "b", "c")), event_id = "survey",
  individual_id = "bird", cell_map = map, dist_breaks = c(0, 25, 75, Inf),
  radius = 75, interval_lengths = c(75, 75), interval_units = "seconds",
  units_in = "m", surveyed = c(TRUE, TRUE, FALSE))
# What happened to each bird
prepared$first[, c("first_interval", "first_distance_bin", "status")]
#>   first_interval first_distance_bin                            status
#> 1              1                  3              first_outside_radius
#> 2              1                  1 retained_first_incomplete_history
# Survey b is an observed zero. Survey c was not surveyed, so it is NA
prepared$yDistance
#>      [,1] [,2]
#> [1,]    1    0
#> [2,]    0    0
#> [3,]   NA   NA
prepared$yRemoval
#>      [,1] [,2]
#> [1,]    1    0
#> [2,]    0    0
#> [3,]   NA   NA
# Both tables are totals of the same first-detection cells
prepared$first_cells
#>      cell1 cell2 cell3 cell4
#> [1,]     1     0     0     0
#> [2,]     0     0     0     0
#> [3,]    NA    NA    NA    NA
